title: Career Roadmap · Phlebotomist
summary: A Phlebotomist collects blood samples safely for laboratory testing, verifies patient identity, labels and transports specimens correctly, and follows infection-control and patient-safety procedures.

facts.Current degree: Recognised phlebotomy training or relevant Medical Laboratory Technology qualification

blocks.label: Recommended stream
blocks.text: Science with Biology is useful; entry requirements depend on the training programme.

blocks.label: Important subjects
blocks.text: Biology, basic chemistry, human anatomy, hygiene and English.

blocks.label: Entrance/admission
blocks.text: Often institution-specific; verify eligibility, course recognition and clinical practice requirements.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Venepuncture, specimen labelling, blood collection tubes, infection control and patient communication.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Careful observation, empathy, accuracy, hygiene and calm communication.

items.text: Recognised Phlebotomy Technician course → Entry-level blood-collection roles, subject to employer and applicable requirements.
DMLT / Diploma in Medical Laboratory Technology → Broader laboratory support roles, including specimen collection where permitted.
B.Sc. Medical Laboratory Technology / Medical Laboratory Science → Broader diagnostic laboratory and further-study opportunities.
First aid and infection-control training → Additional practical preparation; not a substitute for a recognised qualification.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: Course eligibility, scope of practice and requirements for supervised clinical training vary. Confirm these before enrolment.
Choose a programme with documented practical training and an appropriate recognised qualification.

blocks.label: Training stage 1
blocks.text: Anatomy, circulatory system, patient identification and infection prevention.

blocks.label: Training stage 2
blocks.text: Blood-collection techniques, specimen tubes, labelling and transport.

blocks.label: Clinical practice
blocks.text: Supervised venepuncture, specimen handling, sharps disposal and incident reporting.

blocks.label: Career development
blocks.text: Improve patient communication, collection accuracy and specimen-quality control.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Specimen-labelling audit • Blood-collection safety checklist • Sample rejection tracker • Patient waiting-time improvement plan.
The WHO’s phlebotomy guidance emphasises safe blood collection, accurate patient/sample identification, infection prevention and correct specimen transport.

blocks.label: Typical pathway

blocks.text: For example, the American Society for Clinical Pathology offers an international Phlebotomy Technician credential with specific education, training and experience pathways. Certification eligibility does not itself guarantee local employment or work authorisation.
